audit.whatIsWrong: The page disagrees with itself: diff reads HARD while tone is the green favoured colour, diffRating is 4/10, and both breakdown.difficulty and report[14] say 'Favoured matchup'. The win rate is 47.43%.
audit.why: A sub-50% win rate cannot be a favoured matchup. Of the two conflicting statements, the diff enum is the one the data supports, so the rating, tone and prose are what should move.
audit.corrected: diffRating 4/10 -> 7/10, carryRating 5/10 -> 6/10, tone to the hard-matchup orange, and both difficulty strings rewritten to 'Hard matchup'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Sylas all seven rows against a packet chart of Skill/Maokai/Maokai/Skill/Sylas/Sylas/Sylas — and the content whys underneath already describe the opposite: whys[1] says Maokai 'wins the exchange' at 2, whys[2] says you are 'net negative in every short exchange', whys[3] says the lane 'stalemates until 6'. Four rows render a winner the text contradicts.
audit.why: packet.levelChart plus the mirror, which flipped rows 0 and 3 to Skill and rows 1 and 2 to Maokai as one atomic group.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 3 to Skill (5/10), rows 1 and 2 to Maokai (4/10), as matched full/content pairs with all four full-layer whys rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance is described only as a 'point-and-click root — count its cooldown' with no number, and the page never mentions that Maokai is untargetable for the duration of the dash.
audit.why: Kit: W 14/13/12/11/10s, and Riot's text says he 'becomes untargetable and dashes to the target'. That matters concretely — a Chain Lash explosion or a timed Kingslayer aimed at him during the W simply does not connect. Bramble Smash is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s and Nature's Grasp 130/110/90s at 3000 range.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries the 14s and the untargetable window; report[5] carries the W, Q and R timers.

audit.why: The _missing file flags needs-antiheal on Sap Magic, and report[8] already ends with 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain.' The requirement is met.

edits.before: Q poke is your only level-1 tool — chain it on his step-ups but don't force anything; your power arrives with levels.
edits.after: Neither of you has an engage yet — his saplings chip, your Q and passive autos answer, and it stays even.

edits.before: W online — the burst-heal turns even trades into wins. Take the extended trade only when his answer is down.
edits.after: His W root goes live with your E — he presses it the instant your chain lands and wins the exchange.

edits.before: Full kit: E2 chain into Q-W-AA is a real chunk, and E1's shield eats the counter-trade. Trade in full rotations.
edits.after: Full sapling-W-Q kit online, and Sap Magic erases the chip you deal between trades — you go net negative.

edits.before: Weave passive autos between every spell. Trade around Twisted Advance (Root) and bank small HP leads — they compound at 6.
edits.after: His W leaves brief windows, but Sap Magic closes the HP gap as fast as you open it — the lane stalls out until 6.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — Point-and-click root — count its cooldown before stepping up. Check it before every step-up. - E1 shield is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1 and he is untargetable during the dash, so timed burst whiffs; step up only once it is spent. - E1 shield is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.

edits.before: Track Maokai’s Twisted Advance (Root): Point-and-click root — count its cooldown before stepping up. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Maokai’s Twisted Advance: a 14s targeted root, untargetable mid-dash. His Q knocks back on 7s and his R is 130s at rank 1.

notes: The _missing file lists a dash-denied rule claiming Bramble Smash grounds your Kingslayer and Abscond. Riot's own Q description says only that it knocks back nearby enemies, deals magic damage and slows — no grounding. Per the kit-file rule that the description overrides a misfiring flag, I did not write grounding anywhere; if Bramble Smash really does ground, breakdown.cooldowns is where it belongs. Also: breakdown.mid still says 'Respect his E stun before you step in' (per the mirror's note, a fabricated stun on a sapling toss) — it needs a paragraph-length rewrite inside the band and is still outstanding.
